title: Replication Spec: Granger Causality in Expectiles - M-vine copula test
hypothesis: H0: no Granger causality in tau-expectile: E[R_tau(X_t-mu_tau(X_t|I_X))]=E[R_tau(X_t-mu_tau(X_t|I_{X,Z}))] i.e. GC_tau=0 and hat GC_tau not significantly >0; H1: Z Granger-causes X in tau-expectile i.e. E[R_tau with Z] < E[R_tau without Z] i.e. GC_tau>0.
data_sources: Simulated DGPs S1,S2,P1-P4 as defined; Empirical Yahoo Finance S&P500, FTSE100, Nikkei225, SSE Composite, Hang Seng Index; daily  September 2012 - October 2014; Not stated otherwise.
sample: Simulation: stationary strictly stationary k-Markov (k=1) process (X_t,Y_t,Z_t) with d=2, d+1=3 series; 6 DGPs: S1 three independent AR(1) eta ~ N(0,1), S2 three independent GARCH(1,1) with sstd(0,1,nu=5,xi=-1.5), P1 linear AR+ lags, P2/P3/P4 interaction 5*Y_{t-1}Z_{t-1} with Gaussian or GARCH sstd innovations; S=500 Monte Carlo replications per DGP for T=100,200,500. Empirical Global: S&P500 (SP), FTSE100 (FTSE), Nikkei225 (NK) daily Yahoo Finance log-returns r_t=(log(s_t)-log(s_{t-1}))*100, T=500. Empirical Asian: Shanghai Composite (SSE), Hang Seng (HSI), Nikkei225 (NK) daily Yahoo Finance log-returns same transform, T=500. Filters: square-integrable, strictly stationary, Markov order k=1, stationarity via log-returns. Sizes from claims count_S, count_T100, count_T200, count_T500_sim, count_T500_emp.
method: 1. Define tau-th expectile Granger causality measure GC_tau(Z->X)=log( E[R_tau(X_t-mu_tau(X_t|I_X))]/E[R_tau(X_t-mu_tau(X_t|I_{X,Z}))] ) with R_tau(u)=|tau-I{u<0}| u^2 = tau(u)_+^2+(1-tau)(u)_-^2, reduces to GC_mean for tau=0.5.
2. Assume k=1 Markov square-integrable strictly stationary process (X,Z1..Zd). Sample {(x_t,z1_t..zd_t):t=1..T}.

3. Part A: Fit M-vine copula model to M_x=(x_t) via Nagler et al. 2022 selection/estimation; for each t=T0..T generate N=200 i.i.d. predictions {tilde x^{M_x}_{i,t}} of X_t|X_{t-1}=x_{t-1} and compute empirical conditional tau-expectile hat mu_{tau,N}(X_t|X_{t-1}=x_{t-1})=argmin_m sum_{i=1}^N R_tau(tilde x_{i,t}-m).
4. Repeat A1-A2 for M_{x,z}=(x_t,z_t) to get hat mu_{tau,N}(X_t|X_{t-1}=x_{t-1},Z_{t-1}=z_{t-1}).
5. Compute test statistic hat GC_tau(Z->X)=log( sum_{t=T0}^T R_tau(x_t-hat mu_tau(X_t|X_{t-1}))/sum_{t=T0}^T R_tau(x_t-hat mu_tau(X_t|X_{t-1},Z_{t-1})) ), with T0=T/2.

6. Part B p-value: Fit M-vine to full sample M_{x,z}; extract from Tree1 copulas c_{X_t,X_{t+1}} and c_{X_t,Z1,t}; using marginal estimates hat F_X, hat F_{Z1} generate x_t^0 and x_{t+1}^0| x_t^0 and z1_t^0| x_t^0.
7. For i=2..d extract c_{X_t,Zi,t; Z1..Zi-1} from Tree i, using hat F_{Zi} sequentially draw zi,t^0| x_t^0,z1_t^0..zi-1_t^0 to form full vector z_t^0.

8. Using generated sample {(x_t^0,z_t^0):t=1..T} compute hat GC^{0}_tau; repeat B=200 times to get hat GC^{0}_{tau,j} j=1..B; compute p=1/B sum_j I(hat GC^{0}_{tau,j} >= hat GC_tau); reject null of no Granger causality in tau-expectile if p<alpha=0.05.

9. Simulation: tau in {0.1,0.5,0.9} and {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9,0.95} for empirical; S=500 replications; report empirical size/power as rejection rates at alpha=0.05; compare with linear F-test (restricted vs unrestricted AR) and with pairwise M-vine and KNP quantile tests from Balcilar et al.2016.
10. Empirical: apply steps 2-8 with N=200, T0=T/2, B=200, alpha=0.05 to global and Asian indices at stated taus; report bootstrap p-values.
